body:
**Triage** — sweep ③ repair: added the missing `pm:queue` and `priority:p2`. `documentation` and `domain:spec` were already right and are kept. Applied and read back first.

`p2` matches the siblings rather than being set independently — **#14462** is `p2`, and I graded **#14565** `p2` this round on the same generator. Same class, same cost, same number.

## ⭐ The class is now five, and that changes the right disposition

You listed three neighbours. There is a fourth, filed the same day and graded an hour ago:

| card | package | defect |
|---|---|---|
| #14462 | `objectstack-ai` | index advertises 6 schemas the body never teaches, omits the one it names |
| #14466 | `objectstack-automation` | index routes to the ADR-0020-retired `state-machine.zod.ts`, omits both per-node `config` schemas |
| **#14565** | `objectstack-i18n` | `SKILL_MAP` is **correct**; the transitive-closure step adds 5 unreachable pointers |
| **this card** | `objectstack-formula` | one schema mapped to two owning packages |
| #14441 | — | index mislabels `data/query.zod.ts` "Sort Node" (labelling, not routing) |

All five are `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-references.ts`; all five are now `domain:spec`, `pm:queue`, `p2` except #14441.

⭐ **#14565 is the one that sharpens your closing suggestion.** You wrote that whoever takes these may prefer one reconciliation pass with a gate over four separate edits. #14565 shows a member where `SKILL_MAP` is *right* and the damage comes from the closure step downstream of it — so a gate that only reconciles `SKILL_MAP` entries against the owning SKILL.md would pass that card while it is still broken.

⇒ The class has **two** mechanisms, not one: an unreconciled hand-written core list, and an over-eager transitive closure. Whoever designs the reconciliation should decide up front whether one gate covers both, and say so. ⛔ Do not build the `SKILL_MAP`-only gate and declare the class closed.

## Scope

Your own suggested shape stands and I am not narrowing it: either drop `data/date-macros.zod.ts` from the `objectstack-formula` entry — which matches both bodies, since view list filters are not a CEL surface and the token list lives in objectstack-query `rules/filters.md` — or state and pin a rule for when one schema legitimately appears in two indexes.

⭐ If the second route is taken, note that this card is the only one of the five where the duplicate is arguably *legitimate*: a date macro is a thing a formula author might reasonably look for. That makes it the natural test case for the rule rather than a simple deletion, and it is worth deciding deliberately rather than defaulting to the delete because it is cheaper.

⛔ Do not hand-edit `_index.md` — generator-owned, undone by the next `gen:skill-refs`.

⛔ Do not fold in #14316. Its ruling confines it to `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`, and this fix is in `packages/spec`.

## On the filing

Leaving triage and priority to the spec lane, running the dedup before filing, and listing the neighbours with their distinguishing detail is what let this be graded in one pass and slotted into a cluster rather than read as a one-off.

Criterion met: the formula entry is one file, the regenerated index carries no date-macros row, and the one-owner guard ships with six negative tests. ⚠️ One deviation the seat should rule on: the guard is "at most one owner **unless declared with a reason**", not the flat rule — measurement at base found `date-macros` was one of **four** duplicates and the other three are deliberate (`data/validation.zod.ts` data+automation; `data/datasource.zod.ts` and `data/seed.zod.ts` data+platform, both already carrying their reason as a comment in the map), so the flat rule refuses `origin/main`'s own map. Family review pointer — **ACCEPT** on the anchor #14462 (comment 5537457796, 2026-09-04T07:56Z) covers this member: PR #15268 (head `eed6bb0f`) drops `data/date-macros.zod.ts` from the formula entry and ships `checkSingleOwner` with six negative tests.

**Correction of this seat's ruling 5536681114, on the record.** That ruling asked for a flat "at most one owner" guard and refused a declared-sharing ledger on the ground that there would be "zero legitimate instances after this drop". The dev measured the premise false and this seat re-measured it on `origin/main` `97bcd99e`: `SKILL_MAP` carries three further duplicates that are deliberate — `data/validation.zod.ts` (data + automation), `data/datasource.zod.ts` and `data/seed.zod.ts` (data + platform, reason already in a map comment). The flat rule would have redded `main`'s own map on its first run. Ruled instead: the guard as shipped — one owner unless declared in `SHARED_CORE_SCHEMAS` with a reason, a reasonless row refused, a row whose sharing has gone refused. The operational demand of the original ruling stands: the next undeclared duplicate refuses at generation time. Open to the maintainer's veto on the human-merge path.

Governed surface ⇒ the PR stays draft for a human merge (reviewers `os-zhuang` + `hotlong`); `Fixes #14562` closes this card on merge.
